_comment: Clean-arch port-placement gate policy (DATA, not code). ADR-0570. Productizes the defect class #116 exemplified: billing's `AccountingJournalStoragePort` storage-port trait was DEFINED in an in-memory ADAPTER crate, inverting the ports-in-core clean-arch convention proven by tenancy's TenantLifecycleStore and SCIM's UserStore/GroupStore (storage ports live in core/kernel crates; the adapter DEPENDS on core and IMPLEMENTS the port). This gate asserts that no `pub trait <Name>` whose name matches a storage/repository/port heuristic is DEFINED in a crate that (a) lives under a forbidden layer-dir path segment (`adapters`) OR (b) has a crate name ending with a forbidden suffix (`-adapter-inmemory`, etc). The port belongs in a core/ports/kernel crate; the adapter must implement it, not own it. ALL repo-specifics are DATA here: a different repo adopts the gate by repointing port_name_suffixes / forbidden_layer_dirs / forbidden_crate_name_suffixes / allowlist / the frozen baseline; the Rust engine hardcodes no oyatie crate name. The suffix set was calibrated by scanning the live corpus (2026-06-22): Store/Repository/Repo/StoragePort catch the #116 class AND the existing adapter storage ports, while behavioral adapter-internal traits (Authorizer/Backend/Adapter/Spawner/Observer/Provider/Actuator/Evaluator/Sink/Port) are deliberately NOT matched so they never false-positive. Bare `Port` was intentionally excluded: it is too broad and catches behavioral seams (ClockPort, ProviderAuthPort, OperatorAlertPort) that are NOT relocatable storage ports.
_forbidden_crate_name_suffixes_doc: Crate-name suffixes that designate an adapter crate even when the crate does NOT live under a `forbidden_layer_dirs` path segment. Catches adapter-NAMED crates in flat crate trees (e.g. `oya/payroll/crates/oya-payroll-run-storage-adapter-inmemory` is not under any `adapters/` dir but its name ends with `-adapter-inmemory`). Suffix check is applied to the LAST path segment (crate name tail) only.
_port_name_suffixes_doc: Trait-name suffixes that heuristically identify a storage/repository port. Calibrated to be unambiguously storage-shaped. Bare `Port` is intentionally excluded: it is too broad and matches behavioral seams (ClockPort, ProviderAuthPort, OperatorAlertPort) that are not relocatable storage ports.
_min_expected_member_crates_remeasure_20: 800 -> 793. Deletion, not a narrowed scan: this change removes 45 zero-importer libs/ crates outright, so the root workspace member census shrinks with them.
_allowlist_doc: Per-(member_path, trait) carve-outs for a genuine false positive: an adapter-internal trait that is legitimately port-suffix-named but is NOT a relocatable storage port. Each entry is {"member_path": "<repo-relative crate dir>", "trait": "<TraitName>", "reason": "..."}. Shrink-only: an allowlist entry matching no live finding becomes a PP-STALE-ALLOWLIST self-cleaning finding.

product_contract.born_advisory_enforce_no_regression: After #116 fixed billing, the live corpus still carries pre-existing storage-port traits defined in adapter crates (tenant-rbac/session/secret/kms/payroll/hr ports — their relocation is separate per ADR-0570 scope discipline). They are captured in the FROZEN baseline (port-placement-baseline.json). The gate is born-ADVISORY against that baseline and enforces NO REGRESSION: a NEW port-suffix trait defined in an adapter crate (beyond the baseline) fails CLOSED. Baselined entries are ratchet-down only — relocating one is welcome and the gate self-cleans (a baseline entry matching no live finding becomes PP-STALE-BASELINE). The gate flips to fully BLOCKING when the baseline reaches 0.
product_contract.pack_shaped: forbidden_layer_dirs, forbidden_crate_name_suffixes, port_name_suffixes, allowlist, min_expected_member_crates, and the baseline are DATA; the Rust kernel hardcodes no oyatie crate name. A different repo adopts the gate by repointing this policy + baseline.
product_contract.automation: AUTOMATED v1 = flag-with-precise-remediation: each finding names the exact trait, the adapter crate that wrongly defines it, and the sibling core/ports crate it should move to (inferred from the capability stem). A full auto-MOVE codemod (relocate the trait + its port-definitional types into core, rewrite the adapter to depend-and-implement) is a NOTED FOLLOW-UP, not this slice — a trait-relocation codemod is non-trivial and a design act.
product_contract.heuristic_soundness: The suffix set is an over-approximation in the SAFE direction for a born-advisory detector: it can only ever ADD a finding (which the baseline/allowlist absorb), never silently miss the #116 class. Behavioral adapter seams (Authorizer/Backend/Spawner/Observer/Provider/Actuator/Evaluator/Sink) carry none of the storage-port suffixes and are never flagged. Bare `Port` is excluded to avoid flagging behavioral ports (ClockPort, ProviderAuthPort) that are not storage seams.

purpose: Clean-arch port-placement gate. A storage/repository port trait must be DEFINED in a core/ports/kernel crate, not an adapter (the adapter implements it). Covers both adapter-LOCATED crates (path contains a forbidden layer-dir segment) and adapter-NAMED crates (crate name ends with a forbidden suffix). Makes the #116 ports-in-adapter seam-mis-draw class impossible to ship new.
